definition: The structured message types in chat-formatted models.
details: The structured message types in chat-formatted models. The separation exists so models can weight instructions by their source, which underpins both steerability and injection defenses.

explainer.lead: Roles are the structured message types in chat-formatted models, separating instructions by their source. The separation matters because it underpins both steerability and defenses against prompt injection.

tiers.eli5: It's like labelled envelopes: one marked 'instructions from the boss', another 'things a stranger said', so the model knows which to trust more.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers place trusted instructions in system messages and untrusted content in user or tool messages, relying on the model to weight them differently. A pitfall is that models do not always respect the boundary, so injected content can still leak through.
tiers.paperLevel: The structured message types in chat-formatted models exist so models can weight instructions by their source, which underpins both steerability and injection defenses.

explainer.example: A system message sets rules while a user message contains pasted text; the role labels tell the model which should take priority.
